title: Stable excitations and holographic transportation in tensor networks of critical spin chains
abstract: Addresses the stability of hologrons in MERA-based AdS/CFT models. Shows that hologrons (spin-flip bulk excitations X_j|GS>) are unstable during dynamic evolution: P_1^h(t) decays exponentially with lifetime tau ~ 0.5-0.85 (in units of 1/J). Stable bulk excitations with attractive interactions can be constructed from boundary CFT primary operators sigma^boundary_j. Identifies holographic transportation: boundary excitations temporarily vanish and undergo transport along AdS null geodesics through the extra dimension. Observable on Rydberg atom arrays.
key_claims: Hologrons (bulk spin-flip states X_j|GS>) are dynamically unstable: P_1^h(t) decays exponentially with tau ~ 0.51-0.85
Root cause of instability: hologron basis is incomplete — the 2^(L-4) spin-flip states cannot span the full Hilbert space due to 2^4=16 IR degrees of freedom in the core region
Stable bulk quasiparticles are |Psi_j>^{sigma} = U^dag sigma^boundary_j U |GS>, where sigma^boundary_j is the lattice realization of the CFT spin primary operator
The boundary primary operator for H_boundary = (J*L/4pi) sum(X_{j-1}Z_j X_{j+1} - X_j X_{j+1}) is: sigma^boundary_j = V^dag [0.635(X_j + X_{j+1}) - 0.026(X_j Z_{j+1} + Z_j X_{j+1})] V
The unitary V relates H_boundary to H_C-Ising via H_boundary = V^dag H_C-Ising V
Stable quasiparticles exhibit 97.5% probability within primary + first/second derivative descendant subspace at late times
Attractive interactions confirmed: U_int(j,j') < 0 for all measured separations j'=5,6,7,8
Holographic transportation: boundary excitation created by Y_i coupling, vanishes at t~1.5, traverses bulk radially, reappears at t~2.5
Transportation is robust against angular momentum M != 0 and detuning Delta != 0 from criticality
Boundary excitations are generated by space-time localized source: delta_H = -sum_i J_i(t) Y_i with Gaussian profile

hologron_instability_mechanism.what_fails: The n-hologron subspace {X_{j1}...X_{jn}|GS>} cannot span the full Hilbert space because the IR core region has 2^4=16 independent states. The hologron basis only covers the k=0 sector of the generalized basis |Psi^{j1..jn}_{n,k}>. This means energy-conserving transitions out of the 1-hologron subspace into generalized multi-hologron states are always available — there is no large energy gap protecting the 1-hologron sector.
hologron_instability_mechanism.energy_spectrum: Energy ranges of 1-hologron and 2-hologron states overlap substantially. No gap separates the 1-hologron sector from the 2-hologron + IR-excitation sector.
hologron_instability_mechanism.model_dependence: Hologrons ARE stable for H_C-Ising (Chua et al. 2017) because in that model, single spin-flip X_j operators on the boundary ARE the leading-order lattice primary operators of the Ising CFT. The holographic map then guarantees the 1-hologron subspace = primary excitation subspace, which is an eigenspace.
hologron_instability_mechanism.our_model_problem: In the Sahay-Lukin-Cotler model (which we use), H_boundary differs from H_C-Ising. The boundary spin-flip X_j is NOT the primary operator sigma_CFT for this Hamiltonian — it has non-trivial expansion in primary + descendants. So the hologron (bulk X_j flip) does not map cleanly to a primary subspace.

stable_excitation_construction.step1_find_V: Find the unitary V such that H_boundary = V^dag H_C-Ising V. This is given analytically by Evenbly & White (PRL 2016): V = prod_j (i X_j X_{j+1} - I_j I_{j+1}) / sqrt(2).
stable_excitation_construction.step2_sigma_C-Ising: The lattice primary operator for H_C-Ising is known from Zou, Milsted & Vidal (PRL 2020): sigma^{C-Ising}_j = 0.635(X_j + X_{j+1}) - 0.026(X_j Z_{j+1} + Z_j X_{j+1}) + higher order terms
stable_excitation_construction.step3_transform: sigma^boundary_j = V^dag sigma^{C-Ising}_j V (explicit formula in paper Eq.3)
stable_excitation_construction.step4_bulk_state: Single stable quasiparticle: |Psi_j>^{sigma} = U^dag sigma^boundary_j U |GS>
stable_excitation_construction.step5_two_particle: Two-quasiparticle state: |Psi_{j,j'}>^{sigma} = U^dag sigma^boundary_j sigma^boundary_{j'} U |GS>

holographic_transportation.what_it_is: A boundary excitation generated by a spacetime-localized perturbation delta_H = -sum J_i(t) Y_i vanishes from the boundary (the boundary excitation density goes to zero), while the excitation propagates radially inward through the bulk, then reappears on the opposite side of the boundary when the bulk excitation reaches the other boundary.
holographic_transportation.timescale: For Omega=5, sigma_t=sigma_phi=0.4, M=0: excitation emerges at t~0, vanishes at t~1.5, reappears at t~2.5
holographic_transportation.geodesic_interpretation: The parameters Omega and M correspond to energy and angular momentum of null geodesics in AdS bulk. The transportation time is set by the AdS null geodesic traversal time.
holographic_transportation.perturbation_operator: Y_i (not X_i or Ry) — the imaginary Pauli creates the right boundary excitation profile. This is the time-derivative descendant of sigma_CFT.
holographic_transportation.robustness: Persists with M != 0 (angular momentum) and Delta != 0 (off-criticality detuning)

implications_for_our_vqe.why_z2_projection_gave_flat_forces: Our SIM-2026-002 uses Ry(pi/3) single-qubit rotations at bulk sites as hologrons. These are NOT the same as the CFT-motivated sigma^boundary operators. However, the Ry rotations ARE in the tangent space of the hologron (they create superpositions of |0> and |1> at each bulk site). The force profile worked in SIM-2026-002 (no Z2) because the MERA ground state was already optimized and the Ry perturbation has overlap with the correct excitation. When Z2 projection is added (SIM-2026-005), the projection forces the state into the P=+1 sector, which may preferentially project out the hologron content of the Ry excitation, leaving only higher-order components that give flat correlators.
implications_for_our_vqe.deeper_problem: The force profile in SIM-2026-002 measures static energy differences E_2h - 2*E_1h, NOT dynamic stability. So hologron instability does not directly explain the flat force profile. The flat profile in SIM-2026-005 is more likely due to poor VQE convergence (the Z2 projection non-smooth landscape issue documented in MEMORY.md).
implications_for_our_vqe.what_boundary_primaries_would_fix: If we construct quasiparticles using sigma^boundary_j instead of X_j (Ry rotation), the static force measurement U_int(j,j') = <Psi_{j,j'}|H|Psi_{j,j'}> - 2*<Psi_j|H|Psi_j> would use states that are guaranteed to be stable eigenstates (in the thermodynamic limit). This gives a cleaner force profile because the 2-quasiparticle state has well-defined energy with less contamination from multi-particle contributions.
implications_for_our_vqe.circuit_implication: The boundary-primary construction does NOT require VQE at all. It only requires: (1) prepare the MERA ground state |GS>, (2) apply sigma^boundary_j to the boundary qubits, (3) apply U^dag (reverse MERA) to get the bulk quasiparticle state, (4) measure H. This is a pure state preparation + measurement protocol, no variational optimization needed.

circuit_level_changes.current_approach: VQE optimizes MERA circuit parameters to minimize E = <psi|H|psi>. Hologrons are inserted by applying Ry(pi/3) at specific bulk qubit indices after VQE convergence.

new_approach_for_stable_excitations.step1: Keep VQE to find optimal MERA ground state parameters theta_opt (this part is unchanged)
new_approach_for_stable_excitations.step2: Instead of applying Ry at bulk sites, apply the boundary operator sigma^boundary_j to boundary qubits j and j+1. The operator is: 0.635*(X_j + X_{j+1}) - 0.026*(X_j Z_{j+1} + Z_j X_{j+1}) applied as a unitary (must exponentiate or use Givens rotation trick)
new_approach_for_stable_excitations.step3: Apply U^dag (the MERA circuit in reverse) to map boundary excitation to bulk
new_approach_for_stable_excitations.alternative_simpler: Instead of implementing sigma^boundary as a unitary, note that sigma^boundary ~ 0.635*(X_j + X_{j+1}) to leading order. This is just proportional to X_j + X_{j+1} on boundary. In practice: (a) prepare |GS> = U|ground_state>, (b) apply (X_j + X_{j+1}) (unnormalized — need to normalize), (c) apply U^dag, (d) measure energy. The state (X_j + X_{j+1})|GS> / norm IS the boundary primary excitation to leading order.

new_approach_for_holographic_transportat.step2: Apply time-dependent perturbation: evolve under H_boundary + delta_H(t) = H_boundary - sum_i J_i(t) Y_i
new_approach_for_holographic_transportat.step4: Apply U^dag at each time t to reconstruct bulk excitation density rho_i^bulk(t)
new_approach_for_holographic_transportat.key_operator: Y_i perturbation on boundary (not X_i, not Ry in bulk)
new_approach_for_holographic_transportat.what_to_observe: The boundary excitation density should vanish at t~1.5/J and reappear at t~2.5/J for L=16 with J=1, Omega=5, sigma_t=sigma_phi=0.4

hardware_used: theoretical/classical simulation, L=16 boundary chain, exact diagonalization
key_references: Sahay, Lukin, Cotler arXiv:2401.13595 (the paper being studied)
Chua, Passias, Tiwari, Ryu PRB 95, 195152 (2017) — hologrons stable for H_C-Ising
Evenbly & White PRL 116, 140403 (2016) — analytic scale-invariant MERA, gives V unitary
Zou, Milsted, Vidal PRL 124, 040604 (2020) — lattice realization of CFT primary operators
